exposure: Intertwin growth discordance in the absence of fetal growth restriction
cohort: 707 twin pregnancies without fetal growth restriction, categorized as discordant or concordant based on ultrasound between 24 0/7 and 31 6/7 weeks' gestation
finding: Regardless of chorionicity, twin pregnancies with discordance without fetal growth restriction identified on ultrasound between 24 0/7 and 31 6/7 weeks' gestation were nearly twice as likely to develop small-for-gestational-age neonates, deliver earlier in gestation, and experience greater neonatal morbidity than twin pregnancies without discordance.
mod_finding: Pregnancies with growth discordance were more likely to be delivered by cesarean delivery, although this was only statistically significant for dichorionic twin pregnancies.
